A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same attention-indexed model study. Their main text, five figures, equations, references, and appendices A–D support reliable comparison after matching renumbered and relocated content.

before.justification: Section 4 and Figures 1–2 report original AMP, gradient-descent, and averaged-gradient-descent experiments on synthetic data. Appendix D.5 reports additional AMP experiments in Figure 4.

after.justification: Retains the original synthetic-data experiments in Figures 1–2 and the additional AMP experiments in Appendix D.5, Figure 4.

M1.justification: The AIM definition, AMP Algorithm 1, denoisers, and GD/AGD procedures are retained. Appendix C.3 revises the derivation of the existing output-channel equation.

E1.justification: The synthetic Gaussian-input learning tasks and evaluated hardmax and softmax scenarios are unchanged. No dataset, population, domain, or task coverage is added or removed.

E2.justification: Figure 2 retains the same GD and averaged GD comparators alongside AMP and the Bayes-optimal prediction. The linear-channel reference analysis in Appendix D is also retained.

E3.justification: Section 4, figure captions, and Appendix D.8 retain the same data generation, token counts, embedding dimensions, optimization settings, and numerical evaluation procedures.

E4.justification: The width and token-count sweeps, limiting-regime analyses, and recovery-threshold comparisons are retained. No ablation, robustness test, or case study is added or removed.

E5.justification: Figures 1, 2, and 4 retain the reporting of 16 realizations and the same error-bar descriptions. No repeated-run or uncertainty-reporting practice changes.

E6.justification: All five figures retain identical plotted curves, experimental points, and error bars. Numerical thresholds and the reported AMP agreement and GD/AGD findings are unchanged.

T1.justification: Appendix C.3 substantially replaces the derivation of the general output-channel state equation. The inverse-covariance and matrix-square-root differentiation argument becomes an explicit Gaussian construction and covariance-differentiation calculation. The replica power placement is corrected between v2 Eq. 110 and v3 Eq. 119, and previously asserted cancellations are worked out. The final state equation remains the same: v2 Eq. 127 becomes v3 Eq. 140.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and main results retain the same claims about AIM, extensive-width attention, Bayes-optimal predictions, AMP, and averaged gradient descent.

C2.justification: Interpretations of softmax invertibility, hardmax recovery behavior, and GD/AGD performance are unchanged. The stated applicability boundaries and unresolved multi-layer denoising problem are also retained.

D1.justification: Appendix D.8 retains the same code link, PyTorch 1.12.1, Adam learning rate 0.1, initialization and averaging details, and Monte Carlo and iteration settings.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion and reference list are unchanged. Removing the local C.3 citation to [21, 37] leaves the same methodological attribution in the introduction.

P1.justification: Explanatory prose is rewritten and expanded within Appendix C.3. The main narrative and section hierarchy remain intact; other textual changes chiefly concern punctuation, equation references, and the version stamp.

P2.justification: Appendix equations and text reflow, and figure placement changes. Figure 3 now precedes Section D.5, while Figures 4–5 share v3 page 38 instead of separate v2 pages 36–37. Their graphics, dimensions, axes, and legends remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: Appendix C.3 improves the checkability of the existing analysis: v3 Eq. 119 corrects the misplaced replica power in v2 Eq. 110, and explicit Gaussian calculations replace asserted derivative cancellations. These provide a focused gain in mathematical exposition and support, while the overall argument remains heuristic and the results and empirical evidence are unchanged.
